findings.reason: TrieUtils.ts:43-46 declares `index: number`, and lines 54-60 still branch on `typeof index !== 'number'` and compare `'' + uint32Index !== index`. The signature misdescribes the contract. Runtime is unchanged because the callers are still JS, so it stays low.
findings.claim: wrapIndex types index as number, yet its body handles string indices, so that branch narrows index to never and is no longer type-checked.
findings.evidence: Signature `wrapIndex(iter: Collection<unknown, unknown>, index: number): number` is followed by `if (typeof index !== 'number') { const uint32Index = index >>> 0; if ('' + uint32Index !== index ...`. Inside that branch `index` has type `never`, so the string comparison is never checked. Runtime is unchanged because the callers (Seq.js, List.js, Range.js, Stack.js) are still JS.

findings.reason: TrieUtils.ts:68-72 checks `size !== undefined` and `end === undefined`, line 91 checks `index === undefined` and line 23 guards `if (ref)`, yet every parameter is typed as required. Only the types are wrong and callers are still JS, so it stays low.
findings.claim: wholeSlice, resolveBegin, resolveEnd, resolveIndex and SetRef take non-optional parameters even though their bodies handle undefined.
findings.evidence: `wholeSlice(begin: number, end: number, size: number)` checks `size !== undefined` and `end === undefined`. `resolveIndex(index: number, size: number, ...)` checks `index === undefined ? defaultIndex` and `size === undefined`. `SetRef(ref: Ref)` guards `if (ref)`. Callers such as Range.js and Repeat.js pass the `end` from `slice(begin, end)`, which may be undefined.
